### Why I choose Signal:
* **The Gold Standard for Privacy:** Signal uses state-of-the-art end-to-end encryption (the Signal Protocol). No one—not even the company itself, your internet provider, or the government—can read your messages or listen to your calls. 
* **Zero Data Harvesting:** Unlike most tech companies, Signal does not collect your metadata (who you talk to, when, and where). 
* **Non-Profit:** It is run by the non-profit Signal Technology Foundation. It relies on donations, meaning there are no ads, no trackers, and no financial incentive to sell your data.
* **Feature-Rich:** It has everything you actually need: high-quality voice and video calls, disappearing messages, group chats, and file sharing, all wrapped in a clean, bloat-free interface.

**The Only Catch:** The "network effect." Signal has millions of users, but it isn't as ubiquitous as its competitors. You may have to convince some of your friends and family to download it.

***

### If Signal doesn't fit your needs, here is how I would choose based on other categories:

**1. Choose WhatsApp if you need to reach *everyone*.**
* **Why:** With over 2 billion users, almost everyone already has it. It actually uses Signal’s encryption protocol, so the contents of your messages are secure.
* **The Catch:** It is owned by Meta (Facebook). While they can't read your messages, they do collect a massive amount of metadata (your location, contacts, usage habits) to feed into their advertising algorithms.

**2. Choose Telegram if you want the best features and large communities.**
* **Why:** Telegram is incredibly fast, cloud-based, and has the best user interface. It allows for massive group chats (up to 200,000 people), massive file uploads, and fun features like animated stickers and bots.
* **The Catch:** It is **not** end-to-end encrypted by default (only in specific "Secret Chats"). Telegram stores your messages on their servers, meaning if their servers were ever compromised, your data could be read. 

**3. Choose Discord if you are building a community or gaming.**
* **Why:** It is unmatched for voice-chat rooms, screen sharing, and organizing topics into different channels. It has become the default app for gamers, hobbyists, and study groups.
* **The Catch:** It is not built for privacy or one-on-one texting, and it can be highly distracting. 

**Summary:** If you value your privacy and want a secure, reliable app for texting and calling friends and family, download **Signal**.
